precepts.text: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God and no torment touches them; in the sight of the unwise they seem to die, but they are in peace, their hope full of immortality, and God proved them as gold in the furnace and received them as a burnt offering.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
The chosen are “tried as the gold in the fire”, and Wisdom gives more detail. “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Christ said we will be afflicted, so what does no torment mean? That is the lake of fire. That torment will not touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery, And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” Christ said, fear not them which kill the body; fear him who can kill body and soul. Man cannot touch your soul. They seem to die because the body died, but the real man, the real woman, is not dead. We keep falling for Esau's craftiness: it's all over, we're finished. It is not over. They are in peace; that is sleep, rest.

“For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. Jacob's trouble is just a little chastisement. “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us. Everybody says they believe; he will say, let that one get caught early and see what they do. He found them worthy because they confessed Christ before their tormentors.

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the saints is as a burnt offering to the Lord. Christ gave his life, and he said if you will not take up your cross and follow him, you are not worthy of him.

precepts.text: Having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded, for God proved them and found them worthy for himself. What we suffer, God calls a little chastising; endure to the end.
precepts.point: One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. By that measure eighty years is under two hours to God. That is why God calls our trials a small moment.
precepts.why:
We feel what we are going through. We complain, we cry, we fast, we do what we can to make it through. But look what God calls it: “And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. A little chastised. We are not even yet at the point of being persecuted and put to death, and he calls this a little chastising.

That fits with 2 Peter 3:8: if one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, a whole lifetime of suffering is a little chastising, less than two hours in his eyes, and the reward that follows is eternal.

Then, “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” The chastising is the proving. He tries us to find us worthy unto himself. So we have to endure to the end, people. We have to endure to the end, humbling ourselves under his mighty hand, and when the short moment is over, those found worthy will be greatly rewarded.

precepts.text: Once we are purged as gold in the furnace, we shall shine, judge the nations, and have dominion, so prepare the soul for the trials of the purge.
precepts.point: He will lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, and they shall do in Edom according to His anger and His fury. This is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass, for the Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger to perform righteous recompense with our own hands.

note.label: Ezekiel 25: Judgment on Ammon, Moab, Edom, and the Philistines

precepts.why:
Before Israel is the hand of the Most High's vengeance, Israel is tried. “As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.”

Sparks among the stubble: that is the fire of Jacob and the flame of Joseph kindling in the house of Esau. Once we are purged as gold in the furnace, we shall shine. “They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.”

This has not yet come to pass. The Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger, and that comes through the purge. So prepare the soul for the trials of the purge; the gold has to go through the furnace before it shines.

precepts.text: They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth, for grace and mercy is to his saints.
precepts.point: Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
“For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.” Solomon shows where grace and truth are found and who they are for: “They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth: and such as be faithful in love shall abide with him: for grace and mercy is to his saints, and he hath care for his elect.”

Grace and mercy are said in the scriptures to be with his saints. They that put their trust in him understand the truth, and he has care for his elect. The grace and truth that came by Jesus Christ belong to his saints, his elect, the ones faithful in love that abide with him.

points: There shall no torment touch them: it's talking about the lake of fire. In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: this is the same thing we just read in Philippians 1:28.

And their departure is taken for misery: you have a miserable life. What did Brandon Tatum say? Why are you an activist? You have nothing better to do; you're always complaining. Captain Zakar said: Christ was an activist. He was the ultimate activist, always out there preaching and teaching, repent for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. The 12 apostles were activists, if you want to use that word.

And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: you see what God's calling it? A little chastisement. I know for the moment you're in pain, but it's just a little chastisement. For God proved them, and found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering: so the death of the righteous is like a burnt offering to the Lord.
The ungodly which have neglected the righteous shall be punished; their wives are foolish and their children wicked.
